content.text: {"relation":"REFINED","consensus_summary":"All four blind responses converge on a core identification: Sodom and Gomorrah are the Bible's paradigmatic byword for extreme wickedness and sudden, total divine judgment, applicable to any people or city ripe for condemnation. Debate exists only over the specific sin (sexual immorality vs. pride/injustice/inhospitality). Notably, Responses A and C both list as an alternative (minority in A, common in C) the reading that 'Sodom' functions as a prophetic label for apostate Jerusalem, citing Isaiah 1, Jeremiah 23, Ezekiel 16, and Revelation 11:8.","book_summary":"The book identifies Sodom and Gomorrah as 'a spiritual name of Jerusalem': the prophets address Jerusalem's rulers as Sodom (Isa 1:10), Ezekiel calls Sodom Jerusalem's sister and Jerusalem the worse (Ezek 16:46-48), and Revelation applies the name to 'the great city... where also our Lord was crucified' (Rev 11:8). The entry makes this typological identification the sole meaning, cross-referencing a chapter on the Fall of Babylon.","consensus_core_identification":"A universal symbolic byword for consummate wickedness and total, irreversible divine judgment, applicable to any depraved people or city.","book_core_identification":"A spiritual name specifically designating Jerusalem — the apostate covenant city whose corruption exceeds Sodom's and where the Lord was crucified.","core_relation":"BOOK_NARROWS","extension_relation":"BOOK_SUBSET","boundary_disagreement":"The consensus treats Sodom/Gomorrah as a general warning-type applicable to any wicked community (Babylon, Capernaum, towns rejecting the gospel, the ungodly at the eschaton). The book restricts the symbol's referent to Jerusalem alone, elevating what the consensus lists as a minority/secondary alternative (the Jerusalem-as-Sodom typology of Isa 1:9-10, Ezek 16:46-52, Rev 11:8) into the exclusive core identification, and silently dropping the generalized wickedness-and-judgment usage as well as the entire debate over which sin was primary.","material_contradiction":"","rationale":"The book's identification is explicitly anticipated within the consensus itself: Response A's fourth alternative and Response C's third alternative both state that Sodom functions as a typological label for corrupt Jerusalem, citing the same three passages the book prints. The book therefore does not replace the consensus referent with something unrecognized; it selects a recognized strand and narrows the symbol's extension from 'any wicked community' to 'Jerusalem specifically.' Since the consensus's general category (Sodom as a symbolic name applied to a wicked people, especially in prophetic denunciation) remains intact, and the disagreement is over which cases the name covers rather than a contradiction of the same referent, this is REFINED rather than DIVERGENT or NOVEL.","citation_support":"STRONG","strongest_objection":"One could argue the book's move is DIVERGENT rather than REFINED: the consensus core is a general moral archetype, while the book makes Sodom a proper spiritual name of one particular city, effectively replacing an archetype with a specific identification and ignoring the dominant judgment-byword function that pervades both Testaments (Matt 10:15, Luke 17, Jude 7, 2 Pet 2:6). If the book means Sodom refers only to Jerusalem and never functions as a general byword, that could be read as rejecting rather than refining the consensus.","confidence":"high"}
